description.narrative:
Assessment of Project Outcomes - Economy-Wide Effects. The Project is expected to generate approximately 349 direct jobs at the client company, alongside additional indirect employment effects through backward supply chain linkages and induced impacts from increased consumer spending.
Assessment of Contribution to Market Creation - Competitiveness. The IFC investment is expected to enhance the competitiveness of Tanzanias hygiene and personal care sector through demonstration effects that showcase the investment potential of the FMCG sector for other regional and multinational market participants.

IFC is considering a total funding package of up to US$20 million to Movit Products Limited (Movit or the Company or the Borrower), a leading personal care and hygiene manufacturer in Uganda. The Company currently manufactures from its plant in Uganda and sells a wide range of personal care and hygiene products across ten African countries. The funds will be used to i) establish a greenfield manufacturing plant in Tanzania and provide working capital for the new operations under Movit Products (Tanzania) Limited (a co-borrower); and ii) finance equipment purchases and working capital for the Companys Uganda operations (the Project). The new facility will manufacture personal care and hygiene products for the Tanzanian market and neighbouring countries, complementing the Companys existing operations in Uganda. The project is expected to strengthen regional manufacturing capacity, improve access to affordable personal care and hygiene products, reduce reliance on imports, and support job creation and regional value addition in Eastern and Southern Africa.
